The PULL theory of business

PULL generates everything

Mar 06, 2026

The Zen of startups: Before enlightenment, talk to customers and iterate on pull, after enlightenment talk to customers and iterate on pull.

-Josh Valdez (Physics of Startups reader)

In a great market… the market pulls product out of the startup.

-Marc Andreessen (not a Physics of Startups reader… YET)

What is PULL? It is my framework describing a person who has a specific kind of need right now - where, if you offer them something that fits their PULL, they will pull it out of your hands!

Here is the framework:

I think PULL is the missing load-bearing concept in business. In past newsletters, I have suggested that:

  • PULL defines your startup’s Ideal Client Profile

  • PULL is a discovery framework in sales

  • When we know a buyer’s PULL, we know what to sell them

  • PULL defines buyers’ post-sales expectations for the product

  • Startups unfold over time towards true PULL; as markets and technologies change, startups must continue to evolve towards today’s true PULL

  • Intense PULL causes a startup to grow fast; if startups don’t find PULL, they push, and are generally unsuccessful

Let’s put all of these arguments together: PULL generates everything about business.

This is what I humbly present to you as the “PULL theory of business.” (Please clap.)

In action

More specifically, PULL operates like an evolutionary selection mechanism - startups evolve towards PULL, or they die. Survivors fit PULL, as if PULL generated them.

We can see this selection mechanism firsthand in a sales call.

A prospect shows up to talk with us. She has some specific PULL in her mind - for example, “Right now, I am trying to get visibility into when and where my AI features are failing, but my current hand-rolled AI evaluation system is missing too many errors and is too hard to maintain.”

What does she want to hear? “We offer a new kind of AI eval system gives you full visibility and is easy to maintain.”

In other words, something that fits her PULL, using this framework:

If she doesn’t hear this, she doesn’t believe we fit her PULL. And this means she won’t buy. We get ghosted, the deal doesn’t close, the sales cycle drags on forever, etc. Think of these bad things as a kind of evolutionary selection pressure, and we experience this selection pressure whenever we do something that doesn’t fit a buyer’s PULL!

In the sales process, there are two ways to not fit their PULL:

  1. Wrong sequence: For example, jumping straight into a demo before we have articulated what our product is - she is not ready for the demo, she sees screens she struggles to understand, and we lose her!

  2. Right sequence, wrong content: If we describe the above product as “the future of AI evals, with a mixed architecture that blends deterministic and LLM-based scoring,” she’s not going to understand what we’re talking about.

And so: Both the sales process and its contents evolve to fit the buyer’s PULL. (This includes pricing and packaging too, of course!) These things all evolve because they must: When they don’t, we lose deals, which hurts our feelings and we worry about failing - evolutionary selection pressure operates on us, viscerally.

We’ve zoomed in on the sales process, but we can zoom out and see this operating across the entire customer journey. The customer buys our product to help them accomplish their project - the “P” in PULL! If we onboard a customer to the product, and they have a great onboarding experience and the product is delightful to use, but can’t they accomplish their project with it, they churn - again, we experience selection pressure that tells us to fit PULL (or else, feel more pain)!

Finally, this selection pressure operates across customer journeys. When we try to deliver across multiple different kinds of PULL, we find it to be monstrously difficult to do. This pressure leads us to evolve to serve one repeatable case study - find people with near-identical PULL, serve them the same way, and build a “factory” to do that. This is a construct we create and adapt to fit PULL’s evolutionary selection pressure.

So what?

It is easy to avoid the unpleasant feeling of selection pressure. In fact, basically all the modern startup playbooks, with their rabid avoidance of sales, their emphasis on customer interviews and design partners, all actively delay you feeling selection pressure. You feel productive until you experience reality.

Embrace the Zen of startups. PULL is out there, and it will teach you what it wants, if you are willing to listen.
